about.title: Personal Injury Help in Vallejo, California
about.longDescription: Vallejo sits where I-80 meets the Carquinez Strait, and much of daily life here moves along a handful of corridors: Sonoma Boulevard running the length of town, Broadway Street and Tennessee Street threading through the neighborhoods, and the freeway itself carrying commuters toward the bridge. Public records for 2025, the most recent final year, list 439 injury collisions in the city, with 610 people hurt and 19 lives lost. Those same records show reported crashes rising on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when the evening drive home is heaviest. Behind each of those numbers is someone dealing with an emergency room bill, a car that no longer runs, or a job they cannot get back to yet. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not represent you or give legal advice; we connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in Solano County, and that attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether your injury happened on a Mare Island commute, on a sidewalk downtown, or in a store off Sonoma Boulevard, you can reach out, describe what happened, and find out whether a claim is worth pursuing, at no cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Vallejo Claim

items.title: Two years to file, and sometimes far less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county, or state agency may be responsible, a claim can be due in as little as six months, so the calendar matters from day one.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share of the blame, but you are not barred from pursuing a claim.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: For a typical injury claim in California, there is no statutory limit on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. An attorney can explain how these losses are documented.

items.title: Contingency means no fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: The attorneys in our network work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and there is no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Vallejo and the rest of Solano County with an independent personal injury attorney. We do not give legal advice or represent you. The attorney you are connected with handles your case directly.

items.question: Where do collisions in Vallejo tend to happen, according to public records?
items.answer: Public collision counts for Vallejo show the highest volumes along Sonoma Boulevard, I-80, Broadway Street, and Tennessee Street. These are simply the corridors with the most reported incidents, which largely reflects how much traffic they carry. Records also show reported crashes peaking on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a claim over a city-maintained road or a public vehicle, you may need to file a formal claim within six months. Talking with an attorney early helps make sure nothing is missed.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. Your recovery is reduced in proportion to your share of responsibility, but being partly at fault does not eliminate your right to pursue a claim. An attorney can review the facts and explain how fault might be assessed in your situation.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. Our connection service is free, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. You can ask questions and decide whether to move forward without any upfront cost.
